architecture.summary: Documents only: the SO-12 release record docs/implementation/self-onboarding-s2-release.md records the upgrade of the two live production tenants to the released image. Step 11 gets the go-ahead of the owner (about 21:58 UTC on 2 November 2026, "Upgrade tenants") and the result 22:03 to 22:05 UTC: the fleet list of 22:03:44 UTC (2 live rows on sha256:72f51715...), the fleet upgrade --all of 22:04:00 UTC to sha256:515a70f6... in one batch of 2 (dep-dbkghld9fdbs73fkn240 and dep-dbkghmbm8hqs73cgv7s0 live after 28.4 s and 28.5 s, digest recorded, end 22:04:39 UTC), and the checks of 22:04:58 UTC on Render, the registry rows, and the Axiom dataset system-log, with no MCP call. A finding records that the documented fleet.ts list ends with "The tenant registry cannot be read. Nothing changed." from the Mac of the operator, because the default acquisition bound of 1 s is shorter than the TLS connection to the production pooler; the manager ran the list and upgrade commands of the script with the bounds of the rehearsal database reads from a scratch runner, and a follow-up makes the bounds configurable. Production is uniform on the released image, and nothing stays open in step 11. Section 1.2, the end of the TENANT_IMAGE result, item 14 of section 6, and a new row of section 7 follow the change; the tenant fleet runbooks and the fleet section of script/README.md get one sentence each about the SQL bounds. Every fact comes from the brief of the manager session. No source, test, configuration, workflow, migration, or Mermaid block changes; the production architecture is unchanged.
